item.title: Dynamics in a Low-Rank Separable Field Cellular Automaton
item.description: arXiv:2606.08983v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Cellular automata (CA) are widely used to study how simple rules generate life-like behavior, typically through local interactions. Here, we introduce a Separable-Field Cellular Automaton (SFCA), in which conventional local-neighborhood interactions are replaced by updates governed by a normalized global coupling field. Each cell is updated according to q = n/n_max, with survival and birth controlled by threshold intervals S and B. Systematic scans over interval widths and positions revealed four outcome classes: extinction, fixed points, cycles, and long transients. The phase diagram was organized by the relative geometry of S and B: fixed points were enriched when B was contained within S, whereas long transients concentrated near the boundary between partial overlap and no overlap. A fine scan across this transition revealed a narrow long-transient ridge separating two distinct cycle-dominated regimes: a dense, high-change-rate branch approximating global period-2 alternation and a sparse, low-change-rate, stripe-like branch. Damage-spreading analyses were consistent with delayed selection between these cyclic attractor families and provided no evidence for sustained exponential trajectory separation. Finite-size analyses showed that the ridge persists across all tested lattice sizes, although its position shifts systematically with system size. These results show that structured long-lived dynamics can arise under separable global coupling with a field matrix of rank at most one, suggesting that nontrivial collective organization can persist under strongly compressed interaction architectures.
item.dc:creator: Xiaorui Shi, Mengsha Huang

item.title: Local decoders for fault-tolerant quantum computation and translation-invariant stabilizer codes
item.description: arXiv:2609.11457v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct the first fully spatially local fault-tolerant quantum computer based on topological codes in fewer than four spatial dimensions. Our construction is a two-dimensional architecture that uses only geometrically local quantum and classical operations, bounded-speed classical communication and computation, and a constant density of quantum and classical resources. The core component is a new time-translation-invariant cellular-automaton decoder for the surface code. This decoder preserves logical information for a time stretched-exponential in the code distance and operates continuously during state injection, stabilizer-state preparation, lattice surgery, and transversal readout. We also prove that every translation-invariant topological Pauli stabilizer code is locally decodable under phenomenological noise.
item.dc:creator: Nathaniel Selub, Aditya Bhardwaj, Ethan Lake
